_comment: Triage of the mutation runs over include/morph, produced by scripts/mutation.sh.
A survivor is a mutant the suite passed on: the program was changed and no test said so.
That is what the tool reports. `runs[1]` records the measurement, made while working
morph#431 and morph#432, that it is not what the tool means here -- four survivors sampled
from three different headers were hand-applied to the source and every one of them turned
the suite red. See `false_positive_finding` below; read it before treating any single
The classes below still divide the list usefully -- `equivalent` entries are listed
individually with a reason each, because an unexplained exclusion is a suppression, and the
side channels are recorded separately so a future decision about logs is made about logs.
But the residual class is now an upper bound on missing assertions, not a set of them.
Re-measure with: MULL_PREFIX=... bash scripts/mutation.sh core-forms

equivalent.meaning: No test could distinguish the mutant from the original, so the survivor is not a gap. Listed individually below.

entries.reason: The golden-ratio hash_combine mix. Every one of its three additions feeds a value used only as an unordered_map bucket index -- PairKeyHash is never serialised, never compared to a constant, and never pinned in docs/spec/pinned_facts.toml. Turning an addition into a subtraction yields a different hash, and an unordered container is required by the standard to behave correctly under any hash function, so no observable behaviour changes. What a test could assert -- that equal keys hash equally -- the mutant preserves, because it mutates the mixing arithmetic and not the inputs.

Bridge::KeyHash is the same mix over the same kind of value, for _executors' bucket index, and equivalent for the same reason: the hash is internal to one unordered_map in one process and reaches no wire, no file and no assertion.

reserve() is a capacity hint. Its argument affects how many reallocations follow and nothing else -- the vector's contents, size and iteration order are identical whether it is told 42 or the real count. A test that could tell the difference would be asserting on an allocator, which is not part of this API.
A capacity hint on a std::string, equivalent for the same reason as backend.hpp:749.

A capacity hint on a std::vector, equivalent for the same reason as backend.hpp:749.

side_channel_logging.meaning: Removing a log call survives because nothing in morph_tests captures log output.
side_channel_logging.reason: This is not equivalence -- a log line that stops being emitted is an observable change, and morph::log has a sink this suite could install. It is a deliberate absence of assertions on a diagnostic channel, and it is recorded separately from the gaps below so that a future decision to assert on logs (or not to) is made about logs rather than buried in a total.

unasserted.count: see runs[1] and false_positive_finding -- the residual class is an upper bound, not a count
unasserted.meaning: Code morph_tests executes that the report says no test would notice being wrong. Four of these were sampled and hand-applied on 2026-09-03; all four turned the suite red. Treat an entry here as a site to check, not a gap that has been found.

shapes_worth_naming.shape: the server's reply is deleted and the suite passes
shapes_worth_naming.detail: cxx_remove_void_call on reply(wire::encode(makeOk(env.callId, ...))) survives at eight sites in remote.hpp, and on makeErr replies for 'unauthorized', 'connection closed' and 'too many ...' at twelve more. The dispatch paths run; what they put on the wire is not asserted at those sites. The scenario corpus under scripts/scenario asserts wire replies for the ladder rungs, which is why this is invisible to the C++ suite rather than untested everywhere -- but morph_tests is what morph#405 measures.
shapes_worth_naming.status: Disproved on 2026-09-03: the two sampled sites of this shape fail 34 test cases when hand-applied. See false_positive_finding.

shapes_worth_naming.shape: a boundary comparison is only ever exercised away from its boundary
shapes_worth_naming.detail: cxx_gt_to_ge and its family survive on include/morph/core/wire.hpp:514 (the kMaxEnvelopeBytes cap), payload_schema.hpp:169 (kPayloadShapeMaxDepth), forms/instance_constraints.hpp:156 (kMaxDecimalPlaces), forms/forms.hpp:2356 and a dozen more. Each is a comparison tested only at values where moving it by one changes nothing. wire.hpp:514 is the one this run turned into a test -- see tests/test_wire_hardening.cpp, 'decode's size cap is exact at kMaxEnvelopeBytes', whose neighbour was already named 'at the size limit boundary' while asserting a 1 KiB envelope.
shapes_worth_naming.status: Real, and three of them are now closed: payload_schema.hpp's kPayloadShapeMaxDepth comparison, instance_constraints.hpp:156's kMaxDecimalPlaces guard and forms.hpp:2356's offender-list separator are all off the survivor list as of runs[1].

shapes_worth_naming.shape: a completion is never delivered and nothing waits on it
shapes_worth_naming.detail: cxx_remove_void_call on onDone(failure), onDone(nullptr), onDone(std::current_exception()) and resultState->setException(...) survives in backend.hpp and completion.hpp. A test that drives the path without awaiting its completion cannot distinguish a completion that never arrives from one that arrives late.

caveat: The number can only be too high, not too low. tests/test_outbox.cpp names its scratch
file after the address of a stack object, which is stable across processes, so twelve
concurrent copies of morph_tests can collide on it; a collision fails a case, and a
failed case reads to Mull as a killed mutant. It cannot manufacture a survivor, so the
359 below are real and the 640 kills are an upper bound.

results.mutant: cxx_remove_void_call on reply(wire::encode(makeOk(env.callId, {}, mid.v))) and on the fresh-instance sibling
sample_failures: tests/test_coverage_push95.cpp:572 -- envelope decode failed: index 0: no_read_input

consequences: morph#431's headline -- 'twenty places where the framework's response path can be
deleted and morph_tests stays green' -- is false as stated. The response path is
asserted; deleting it turns 34 cases red.
The 64.06% and 64.76% scores are lower bounds on the suite's real mutation score, and
the survivor list is an upper bound on the set of missing assertions. The caveat
recorded for the baseline run said the score 'can only be too high, never too low';
that was about test_outbox.cpp's scratch-file collisions and remains true of that
mechanism, but this one pushes the other way and is much larger.
cxx_remove_void_call is 148 of the 352 survivors, and remote.hpp and bridge.hpp -- both
header-only and included by many of morph_tests' 105 translation units -- are 211 of
them. Neither number should be read as a gap count until this is understood.
mechanism: Inferred from the shape of the result, not verified. Every affected site is in a header
compiled into many translation units, where each object carries its own copy of the
function and the linker keeps one. Mull embeds its mutants per object (the
`.mull_mutants` section) and the runner enables one by id; if the copy carrying the
enabled mutant is one the linker discarded, the running program is unmutated and the
mutant is scored as a survivor. That would make the effect specific to header-defined
code in a multi-TU binary, which matches where the survivors are concentrated -- but
it has not been confirmed against Mull's implementation.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A run in which a hand-applied survivor leaves the suite green would show that survivor
to be a real gap. Sampling four and finding four false positives does not prove all 352
are; it proves the report cannot be read site-by-site without this check.
Confirming the mechanism (or finding a Mull option that avoids it -- a single-TU
